meaningEn: The social radar — reading a room and sensing others' needs; it's a skill you're judged on.
exampleKo: 저 친구는 눈치가 빨라서 분위기를 잘 읽어.
exampleEn: That friend is quick to pick up on things, so they read the room well.

meaningEn: Attachment that builds between people (or things) over time — not romantic love, but a deep bond.
exampleKo: 오래 같이 살면 가족끼리 정이 많이 들어요.
exampleEn: When you live together a long time, families grow very attached to each other.

meaningEn: 'Our' used where English says 'my' (our mom, our house) to mark belonging to a shared group.
exampleKo: 우리 엄마는 요리를 정말 잘하세요.
exampleEn: My mom is a really good cook.

meaningEn: Loyalty owed to those who stood by you — a strong moral obligation to return that support.
exampleKo: 우리 둘은 의리로 뭉쳤으니까 배신하면 안 돼.
exampleEn: We're bound by loyalty, so don't betray me.

meaningEn: Being in debt for someone's help — a discomfort Koreans track carefully to repay.
exampleKo: 지난번에 신세를 져서 이번에는 제가 밥 살게요.
exampleEn: I was in your debt last time, so I'll buy dinner this time.

meaningEn: To look after someone's needs by noticing them and acting, without being asked.
exampleKo: 엄마는 항상 내 도시락이랑 약을 챙겨주셨어.
exampleEn: Mom always packed my lunch and remembered my medicine for me.

meaningEn: Warm and attentive in how one speaks and treats you — affectionate without being sappy.
exampleKo: 우리 할머니는 누구에게나 살갑게 대해주셔서 좋아요.
exampleEn: I like how my grandma is warm and kind to everyone.

meaningEn: Brusque and undemonstrative, showing no warmth on the surface — but not unkind.
exampleKo: 우리 아빠는 무뚝뚝하지만 속은 따뜻한 분이세요.
exampleEn: My dad is gruff, but he's warm-hearted inside.

meaningEn: To be shy and stiff around people one doesn't know yet — often said of babies too.
exampleKo: 우리 아기는 낯을 가려서 처음 보는 사람한테는 잘 안 웃어.
exampleEn: Our baby is shy with strangers, so she doesn't smile much at people she's just met.

meaningEn: To grow attached to a person, place, or object through time spent together.
exampleKo: 이 동네에 10년 넘게 살았더니 정이 많이 들었어.
exampleEn: I've lived in this neighborhood for over 10 years, so I've grown very attached to it.

meaningEn: Accumulated, unresolved grief and resentment carried over time — sorrow hardened into endurance.
exampleKo: 그 할머니의 얼굴에는 평생 쌓인 한이 느껴졌다.
exampleEn: On that grandma's face, you could feel the accumulated grief of a lifetime.

meaningEn: Chest-tight frustration at something that won't move — a slow explanation, blocked plan, or stuffy air.
exampleKo: 설명이 너무 답답해서 제가 직접 할게요.
exampleEn: The explanation is so frustratingly slow, I'll just do it myself.

meaningEn: The anguish of being wrongly blamed or punished unfairly — it describes how it feels inside.
exampleKo: 난 아무것도 안 했는데 오해받으니 너무 억울해.
exampleEn: I didn't do anything, so it feels so unfair to be misunderstood.

meaningEn: Mild regret that something good ended too soon or fell just short — wistful, not sad.
exampleKo: 벌써 집에 가야 하다니 아쉽다. 좀 더 놀고 싶은데.
exampleEn: I have to go home already, what a shame. I want to play a bit more.

meaningEn: Quietly hurt that someone close didn't do as much as you'd hoped — it stings precisely because you care.
exampleKo: 네가 내 생일도 잊어버려서 좀 서운했어.
exampleEn: I was a bit hurt that you even forgot my birthday.

meaningEn: The fluttery anticipation before something good — it's the physical flutter itself, common in early romance.
exampleKo: 내일 여행 갈 생각에 아침부터 너무 설레.
exampleEn: I'm so fluttery with anticipation for the trip tomorrow, I've been like this since morning.

meaningEn: The warm, swelling feeling in your chest when proud of what you or someone close achieved — quieter than 'proud'.
exampleKo: 시험에 합격해서 너무 뿌듯하고 기분 좋아.
exampleEn: I'm so proud and happy that I passed the exam.

meaningEn: Relieved and sad at once — like graduation or a last day at work; two feelings fused.
exampleKo: 학교 졸업하고 나니 시원섭섭한 기분이 들었어.
exampleEn: After graduating from school, I felt relieved and sad at the same time.

meaningEn: To sulk over a small slight and show it, expecting to be coaxed back.
exampleKo: 내가 장난쳤다고 삐쳤어? 빨리 풀어.
exampleEn: Are you sulking because I played a prank? Cheer up quickly.

meaningEn: A tender ache of pity or sympathy — like watching an aging parent work hard; softer than 'heartbreaking'.
exampleKo: 혼자 힘들게 일하는 모습이 너무 짠해서 도와주고 싶었어.
exampleEn: Their struggling to work alone made me feel such tender pity that I wanted to help.

meaningEn: Heartsore — upset in a way that gnaws at you, over something gone wrong or someone you care about.
exampleKo: 친구랑 다투고 나니 너무 속상해서 잠이 안 와.
exampleEn: After fighting with my friend, I'm so heartsore I can't sleep.

meaningEn: A physical illness brought on by anger and grief suppressed for years — recognized in Korean medicine.
exampleKo: 그 할머니는 오랫동안 쌓인 스트레스로 화병을 앓고 계셨어.
exampleEn: That grandma had been suffering from hwabyeong after years of bottled-up stress.

meaningEn: A feeling of satisfying relief — whether from cool air, hot soup, a good massage, or a problem resolved.
exampleKo: 이 얼큰한 국물 마시니까 속이 시원하다!
exampleEn: Drinking this spicy soup gives me such a satisfying feeling of relief!

meaningEn: The clean, light feeling after a shower, good sleep, or resolving something that was bothering you.
exampleKo: 뜨거운 물로 샤워하고 나니 몸이 개운해졌어.
exampleEn: After taking a hot shower, my body feels clean and refreshed.

meaningEn: Heavy and greasy in a way that coats the mouth (food) — also, a person who is cheesy or overly smooth.
exampleKo: 이 피자는 너무 느끼해서 김치랑 같이 먹어야겠어.
exampleEn: This pizza is too greasy; I need to eat it with kimchi.

meaningEn: Nutty, toasty savouriness — also the quiet glee at seeing someone who wronged you get their due
exampleKo: 참기름 냄새가 진짜 고소하고 맛있지 않아?
exampleEn: Doesn't sesame oil smell really nutty and delicious?

meaningEn: Food that is clean and light on the palate, not rich. Also, a person's plain, unpretentious manner.
exampleKo: 이 국물은 담백해서 해장하기 딱 좋아.
exampleEn: This broth is clean and light, perfect for a hangover cure.

meaningEn: Deliberately cute, endearing behavior used to charm others — a social skill, not just cuteness.
exampleKo: 너 애교 부리면 뭐든지 다 해줄 것 같아.
exampleEn: If you act cute, it feels like I'd do anything for you.

meaningEn: Babyish, clingy acting-up to someone who dotes on you, usually for attention or a favor.
exampleKo: 막내라서 어리광이 좀 심한 편이야.
exampleEn: Since she's the youngest, she tends to act a bit too babyish.

meaningEn: Shamelessly playing innocent while knowing exactly what you're doing, keeping a straight face.
exampleKo: 걔는 뭘 해도 능청스러워서 믿을 수가 없어.
exampleEn: No matter what he does, he's so shamelessly sly, I can't trust him.

meaningEn: Uninvited meddling in other people's business — often implying being nosy or overstepping.
exampleKo: 내 일에 오지랖 좀 부리지 마! 네 일이나 신경 써.
exampleEn: Stop meddling in my business! Mind your own.

meaningEn: Immature for one's age, lacking common sense or emotional maturity.
exampleKo: 걔는 나이만 먹었지 아직도 너무 철없는 행동을 해.
exampleEn: He's old enough, but he still acts so immature.

meaningEn: Subtly, more than you'd expect or admit — often used to soften a compliment or complaint.
exampleKo: 이 카페 커피 은근히 맛있더라. 또 가자!
exampleEn: The coffee at this cafe was surprisingly good, actually. Let's go again!

meaningEn: Forcing yourself, or being forced, to do something against your will.
exampleKo: 하기 싫은데 억지로 하려니까 너무 힘들다.
exampleEn: It's so hard trying to force myself to do something I don't want to.

meaningEn: Roughly, good-enough, without full effort — can be practical or a criticism.
exampleKo: 숙제 대충 하지 말고 좀 더 신경 써서 해 봐.
exampleEn: Don't do your homework roughly; try to put more effort into it.

meaningEn: Abuse of power by someone in a stronger position, like a boss to staff or client to vendor.
exampleKo: 저 사장님은 직원들한테 갑질이 너무 심해.
exampleEn: That boss's abuse of power towards his employees is too severe.

meaningEn: An after-work team dinner, usually with drinking, for team bonding — often effectively compulsory.
exampleKo: 오늘 회식 있다고? 나 오늘 약속 있는데 어쩌지?
exampleEn: There's a team dinner today? I have plans, what should I do?

meaningEn: 'An eye-stamp' — showing your face so a key person registers you were there.
exampleKo: 사장님한테 눈도장 찍으려면 일찍 출근해야 해.
exampleEn: If you want the boss to notice you, you have to come to work early.

meaningEn: Reacting to news everyone else processed long ago — being late to the party, often said teasingly.
exampleKo: 그거 벌써 지난주 뉴스인데 이제 와서 뒷북치냐?
exampleEn: That was last week's news; are you just now reacting to it?

meaningEn: So hectic there's no headspace left; frazzled or all over the place — for a day, room, or person.
exampleKo: 오늘 하루 종일 너무 정신없어서 점심도 못 먹었어.
exampleEn: I was so frazzled all day today that I couldn't even eat lunch.

meaningEn: To put in effort, but mainly used as a polite farewell like 'thank you for your work today'.
exampleKo: 오늘 하루도 수고하셨습니다! 조심히 들어가세요.
exampleEn: Thank you for your hard work today! Please go home safely.

meaningEn: 'As you see fit', on your own judgment — warm or cold depending entirely on tone
exampleKo: 점심 뭐 먹을지 알아서 시켜 먹어. 난 아무거나 괜찮아.
exampleEn: Order whatever you see fit for lunch; anything is fine with me.

meaningEn: Talking about someone behind their back after the fact — often implying badmouthing.
exampleKo: 남 뒷담화 하지 말고 직접 가서 말해봐.
exampleEn: Don't talk about people behind their backs; go tell them directly.

meaningEn: To treat everyone to a meal or drinks because something good happened to you.
exampleKo: 나 승진했어! 오늘 저녁은 내가 한턱낼게!
exampleEn: I got promoted! I'll treat everyone to dinner tonight!

meaningEn: 'Rice strength' — the belief that stamina and resilience come from eating proper meals.
exampleKo: 역시 한국인은 밥심이지! 밥 먹어야 힘이 나지.
exampleEn: Koreans truly live on 'rice strength'! You only get energy after eating rice.

meaningEn: Being the same age as someone — in Korea, this instantly settles speech level and closeness.
exampleKo: 우리 동갑이니까 말 편하게 해도 돼.
exampleEn: We're the same age, so you can speak casually to me.

meaningEn: A housewarming party where guests traditionally bring detergent or toilet paper for good luck.
exampleKo: 우리 다음 주에 집들이 하는데 놀러 올래?
exampleEn: We're having a housewarming next week, want to come?

meaningEn: Eating specific restorative foods like samgyetang to rebuild the body's strength.
exampleKo: 여름이라 몸보신 좀 해야겠어. 삼계탕 먹으러 갈까?
exampleEn: It's summer, so I should rebuild my strength. Shall we go eat samgyetang?

meaningEn: Exaggerating how hurt or tired you are to get sympathy — can be affectionate or dismissive.
exampleKo: 쟤 또 엄살 부리네. 그렇게 아픈 거 아닌 것 같은데.
exampleEn: He's exaggerating again. It doesn't seem like he's that hurt.

meaningEn: Open-handed generosity, especially giving a little extra unasked — like a market vendor's free gift.
exampleKo: 이 동네는 인심이 좋아서 덤을 많이 줘.
exampleEn: This neighborhood is generous, so they give a lot of free extras.
